item.title: 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game
item.description: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains how new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino will prepare for Sunday's game against Liverpool after only a few days with his squad.

item.title: Spurs 'a match for anyone' as win at Man City boosts European hopes
item.description: With the Women's Super League big four firmly established, and London City Lionesses spending their way into European contention, Champions League dreams could have seemed more fanciful than ever for Tottenham Hotspur. But they are firmly in the mix.

item.title: 'Not the right time' - Fernandes pauses Man Utd contract talks
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future.

item.title: Watford seek sixth manager in 18 months after sacking Dionisi
item.description: Watford sack head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games in charge.

item.title: PSG's Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL
item.description: Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.

item.title: Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999
item.description: Noah Okafor scores twice to deliver Leeds United's first win at Chelsea in 27 years, in an impressive 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge. Daniel Farke's side move up to sixth in the Premier League.

item.title: Arsenal go six points clear after lively draw at Newcastle
item.description: Noni Madueke's second-half goal earns Arsenal a 2-2 draw against Newcastle United at St James' Park, as the reigning champions move six points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

item.title: Teenager Williams-Barnett shines as Spurs beat Ipswich
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur teenager Luca Williams-Barnett starres for Roberto de Zerbi's side as they comfortably beat Ipswich Town.

item.title: Coventry beat Palace in Frank's first game after late own goal
item.description: A Dwight McNeil own goal in the 85th minute gives Coventry City a 3-2 win to move three points clear of the relegation zone, as Thomas Frank's first game in charge at Crystal Palace ends in defeat in the Premier League.

item.title: Man City drop points to Fulham despite superb Anderson volley
item.description: Elliot Anderson's fantastic volley earns Manchester City a first Premier League point in over a month as they come from behind to hold Fulham.

item.title: Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth beat Forest
item.description: Evanilson scores in his sixth consecutive Premier League game, as Bournemouth defeat Nottingham Forest 2-0 at the Vitality Stadium.

item.title: Villa's home woes continue as Sunderland earn point
item.description: Aston Villa's struggles at home this season continue as they are held to a goalless draw by Sunderland in the Premier League.

item.title: Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?
item.description: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is set to have a scan on his shoulder after going off injured during Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle.

item.title: Frick delivers on 'heavy metal football' promise
item.description: Mario Frick aimed for "heavy metal football" after taking over from Aberdeen and travelling fans were served up quite the concert at Rugby Park.

item.title: Who am I? Plus today's other quizzes
item.description: Test your football knowledge against today's Who Am I?, Five in Five and Brainteaser.

item.title: Argentina midfielder Paredes collapses during TV interview
item.description: World Cup winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapses while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors.

item.title: Why Arsenal are behind in race for Champions League spots
item.description: Arsenal were open about their aim to win the WSL this season but they find themselves well adrift - where have things gone wrong?

item.title: I wish referee had opportunity to see 'handball' again - Hart
item.description: Match of the Day pundits Joe Hart and Alan Shearer disagree with Morgan Rogers being penalised for handball, as the Chelsea forward "didn't make himself bigger" with the use of his arms in his side's 4-1 defeat to Leeds United in the Premier League.

item.title: London City keep up title hunt with emphatic win over Crystal Palace
item.description: London City Lionesses stay in the hunt for the Women's Super League title, with a statement second-half performance to give them a 6-2 win over Crystal Palace.

item.title: 'Unbelievable' - how Spurs teenager Williams-Barnett impressed on first start
item.description: Match of the Day pundit Joe Hart explains how teenager Luca Williams-Barnett caused problems for Ipswich Town on his first Premier League start for Tottenham in their 2-0 home win.

item.title: Keating stars as Liverpool hold high-flying Chelsea to goalless draw
item.description: Chelsea miss the chance to consolidate their lead over Manchester City at the top of the Women's Super League as they fail to breach a stubborn Liverpool at the sunny St Helen's Stadium.

item.title: Leeds 'created piece of history' in Chelsea win - Farke
item.description: Leeds United manager Daniel Farke is delighted his side "created a piece of history" following their 4-1 win against Chelsea, their first at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

item.title: 'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

item.title: 'The world got to see today' - Williams-Barnett announces himself as Spurs star

item.title: Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

item.title: AC Milan monitoring Man Utd's Fernandes - Sunday's gossip

item.title: 'We lost two points' - Arteta on 'unacceptable' Newcastle draw
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says his side squandered the chance to take all three points after their 2-2 draw against Newcastle United at St James' Park. The result sees the reigning Premier League champions go six points clear at the top of the table.

item.title: Williams-Barnett's talent bigger than performance - De Zerbi
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi is full of praise for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett who was at the heart of a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town.

item.title: 'It's quite clear' - Maresca believes Haaland goal should have stood

item.title: 'It's a deserved defeat' - Glasner on Bournemouth loss
item.description: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner believes his side "deserved" to lose against Bournemouth as a 2-0 defeat leaves them above the drop zone on goal difference.

item.title: Bayern draw with Cologne as Kane picks up ankle injury
item.description: England captain Harry Kane will be out "for the next few months" after undergoing surgery on torn ankle ligaments sustained during Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne on Friday.
